column1: # expect: allow or pass, by the Bash() rules in permissions.allow of the global settings.
# Rules are matched as shell globs, and a trailing " *" also matches the bare
# command, as the docs say. This checks the rule text, not Claude Code's matcher.
# Claude Code checks deny, then ask, then allow, so a command in ask.tsv still asks.
# Commands in sandbox.excludedCommands run outside the sandbox, so they need
# an allow rule to go without a prompt. --hard, --merge, and --keep ask
# gh api reads without a prompt. The forms that can write ask (ask.tsv)
# git stash runs outside the sandbox. push and pop keep the changes; drop and
# gh reads of runs and checks
# Text tools that read stdin and print, so a pipe of them goes without a
# prompt. sort -o and base64 -o write a file and ask (ask.tsv)
# awk and sed can write files or run commands, xargs runs any command, and
# uniq with operands writes the second one
# echo prints the status of the command before it.
# Not checked here whether Claude Code's matcher takes $? as plain text
